title: Sell Mineral Rights in Jewett, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Jewett, OH
metaDescription: Jewett sits in Harrison County, deep in the Utica/Point Pleasant core. See what dense drilling activity here means for your mineral interest.
heroLead: Jewett sits in a part of Harrison County where drilling has run so continuously that most mineral owners here can find real royalty data somewhere in the family paperwork.
intro: Jewett is a village in Harrison County, positioned within one of the most heavily developed corners of the Utica/Point Pleasant play since operators first proved the play out in the early 2010s. Coal mining and farming shaped the area's economy for generations before shale drilling, and mineral ownership around Jewett is often fractionated across multiple heirs from original farm and coal-company transactions decades old.

sections.heading: What dense drilling around Jewett means for valuation
paragraphs: Given how extensively Harrison County has been developed, a tract near Jewett has a strong chance of already sitting inside a producing spacing unit, sometimes more than one if the operator drilled additional laterals from a different pad years later. Royalty statements and division orders, where they exist, give the most accurate picture of value since they show real production and your exact decimal share directly.

sections.heading: Sorting coal-era severances from Utica-era leases
paragraphs: Many Jewett-area deeds separated coal rights from oil and gas rights decades before shale drilling arrived, sometimes to entirely different parties, so confirming exactly what your family's reservation covers requires reading the original severance deed at the Harrison County Recorder's office in Cadiz rather than assuming based on general area history.

faqs.question: Is Jewett in a heavily drilled part of Harrison County?
faqs.answer: Much of Harrison County has seen dense Utica/Point Pleasant development, and Jewett sits within that activity, though it varies by specific spacing unit.

faqs.question: Could my interest be split between coal rights and oil and gas rights?
faqs.answer: It's possible, since coal was often severed separately from oil and gas in this area decades ago. The original severance deed will clarify what was actually reserved and to whom.

faqs.question: What if I've never received a royalty check but believe I'm an heir to minerals here?
faqs.answer: You may not be properly identified on the current division order, or your interest may sit in a unit that hasn't started producing. A title search will clarify which applies.

faqs.question: What documents help establish my exact decimal interest?
faqs.answer: Your deed, any lease or division order, and recent royalty statements if you have them, which together confirm net mineral acres and current decimal share.

faqs.question: Do I need to sell my entire interest, or can I sell just part of it?
faqs.answer: Most owners can sell all or a portion of their net mineral acres, sometimes limiting a sale to the interest under one specific well or unit while retaining the rest.
